name: Hypothesis PDF anchoring
what_it_is: Hypothes.is client logic for describing and re-anchoring PDF text selections and manual shapes. Current source combines quote, position, and page selectors for text, and page plus PDF-user-space shape selectors for regions or points.
render_model: Hybrid PDF.js integration: extracted page text supports search and position anchoring; the PDF.js DOM text layer supplies ranges and highlights; shape anchors are converted between PDF user space and normalized page-relative viewport coordinates.
annotation_support: Application overlay and remote annotation model. Text anchors use TextQuoteSelector, TextPositionSelector, and PageSelector; current shape tools use PageSelector plus ShapeSelector rather than writing ISO 32000 annotation dictionaries into the PDF.
coordinate_space: TextPositionSelector uses UTF-16 offsets in document textContent. PageSelector uses a zero-based page index. ShapeSelector uses natural PDF user-space points with a bottom-left origin, anchored to a page, and may retain the page view box.
desktop_fit: Strong as an anchoring reference: try position first, verify the exact quote, fall back to quote and context matching, and translate extracted-text offsets to rendered text-layer offsets.
mobile_fit: Good as a data-model reference because selectors do not depend on desktop CSS pixels. Hypothesis client interaction details are not a direct mobile UI prescription for Jevsume.
overlay_chat_fit: Strong: selector-backed anchors remain separate from annotation bodies and replies, allowing a pin or highlight to open a thread without modifying the source PDF.
license: BSD 2-Clause for the Hypothesis client, with separately licensed subcomponents documented in its LICENSE file.
already_in_repo: No Hypothesis dependency or selector model is present. Jevsume already has analogous flattened start/end finding spans, so it can adopt the redundant position-plus-quote anchoring pattern without embedding the Hypothesis client.
risks: PDF text extraction order and normalization vary by viewer and PDF.js version; repeated short quotes can match the wrong occurrence; text-layer and extraction strings can differ; quote search across many pages can be expensive; current upstream main may differ from a deployed Hypothesis release.
recommendation: consider — adopt the redundant selectors and safe fallback strategy, including page hints and Unicode/whitespace alignment, but keep a smaller Jevsume-owned model and mark ambiguous anchors orphaned.
uncertain: The current source supports ShapeSelector, while the older PDF-region design issue says bounding boxes were not captured as of January 2024; deployed versions may lag current main.
Jevsume has not specified how much prefix and suffix context to store or the confidence threshold for accepting a quote fallback.
Cross-viewer portability of PDF text quote and position selectors remains inherently document-dependent.
